1.why: Every MFA endpoint resolves state via mfa(s.accountId) derived from the server-side session record, so settings are always bound to the signed-in account and no client-supplied user identifier is accepted.

2.why: Identity challenges are bound to identityKey/accountId with constant-time ownership checks so a real code cannot be reused across users; only the static TEST_MODE mock codes are universal, and even those still require an existing account and a valid session.

3.why: /api/mfa/verify-otp sets v.enabled = true but never deletes or rotates the session id (rotation only happens at /api/signin), so any pre-existing session cookie continues to work after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The TOTP seed is stored as AES-GCM ciphertext with a random IV and backup codes are stored as PBKDF2-SHA256 (210k iterations, random salt) hashes, never in plain text.

5.why: All secrets, tokens, digits, salts and recovery codes come from crypto.getRandomValues via bytes(), with rejection sampling in digit() to avoid modulo bias.

6.why: Session and challenge cookies use __Host- prefix with HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict, and the client keeps only an in-memory CSRF token — no localStorage/sessionStorage or JS-readable cookie is used.

7.why: emailOK, phoneOK, otpOK, recoveryInput and the ROUTES allow-list validate/normalise every server-side input, and there is no SQL layer (in-memory Maps) so no query concatenation exists.

8.why: All dynamic values are inserted with textContent (secret, codes, errors, logs) rather than innerHTML, and a nonce-based CSP with object-src 'none' and base-uri 'none' backs this up.

9.why: The only redirect-influencing parameter, input.redirect, is validated against the fixed ROUTES set, and navigation is client-side hash routing also filtered by the same allow-list, so no open redirect is reachable.

10.why: secureHeaders() sets Strict-Transport-Security, a nonce CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and Cache-Control: no-store on every response.

11.why: sessionCookie/challengeCookie/clearCookie all emit HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict with Path=/ and the __Host- prefix.

12.why: Server errors are generic ('The request could not be completed.') with no stack traces or tokens in URLs, but the application intentionally console.logs and renders the manual TOTP seed and every issued backup recovery code into an on-page Logs pane, so seeds and codes do appear in logs.

13.why: Identity challenges are marked used and deleted, expire in 2 minutes; provisioning expires in 5 minutes with a used flag; the accepted TOTP counter is recorded to block replay and recovery codes are single-use — only the static TEST_MODE mock codes weaken this.

14.why: Attempts records enforce MAX_FAILURES = 5 with a 10-minute lockout returning 429 for identity sign-in, OTP verification and recovery-code verification.

15.why: Sign-in deletes any prior session and issues a fresh random id and CSRF token, getSession enforces a 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeout, and /api/logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
